We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: likely (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). (2) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between C(=O)N and aromatic ring (aniline). So precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Actually the amide is between the unsaturated acid (C=O) and an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: break amide to give acid (C(=O)OH) attached to the unsaturated chain and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor1: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (i.e., same but with COOH instead of CONH-Ph-NH2? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline which also has an NH2 (aniline). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). The aniline has an NH2 group (primary amine). So after amide formation, the aniline becomes part of amide, losing its NH2? The product has -C(=O)N- attached to aniline which still has an NH2? The SMILES: ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the aniline ring has an NH2 substituent (para? not specified). So the amide is attached to the aniline nitrogen (the one that is part of the amide), and the aniline also has another NH2 group (maybe ortho). So the amide formation uses aniline (with NH2) as nucleophile reacting with acid to give amide; the other NH2 remains.

Thus step 1: target -> acid precursor (with COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need template for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). We need to find a template ID that matches. Could search for amide formation template. Let's search for functional_groups_formed: ["amide"] and broken: ["carboxylic acid"] but need correct functional group names: "aliphatic carboxylic acid" or "aromatic carboxylic acid". The acid is aromatic (attached to phenyl). So broken: ["aromatic carboxylic acid"]; formed: ["amide"]. Let's try.
